introduction.text_001: Built by a director, for directors and teachers.
introduction.text_002: Program Partner started as one band director's answer to the paperwork that ate his planning periods.

story.text_004: Trey English, founder of Program Partner
story.text_007: I've spent my whole career on the music side of the room. I've taught band and choir, music directed school and community theatre productions, taught at the college level, and run a private studio. Today I'm director of bands at Feagin Mill Middle School, adjunct professor of trombone at Mercer University, music director for the Warner Robins High School theatre department and Theatre Macon, and pianist at Mount Zion Baptist Church.
story.text_008: Every one of those roles came with the same second job: fees and balances, forms, inventory, the music library, messages home, schedules. It's the work that keeps a program running, and it usually happens after the students go home.
story.text_009: Program Partner started as a way to keep my own program organized. One May, I was sitting in my office already thinking about the work it takes to get ready for a new school year. My summer and pre-planning to-do lists were ready to go. When I started working through them and found myself opening more than ten spreadsheets, Google Docs and forms, I knew it was time for something better. Once it was working for us, colleagues started asking about it, including a theatre director, a friend with a private flute studio, and directors at other levels.
story.text_010: I didn't build it alone. A few wonderful former music educators who now write software helped me a ton. They know what a rehearsal room feels like and what a director's week looks like.
story.text_011: Program Partner is built for band, orchestra, choir, theatre and private studios. It's designed the way I'd want it as a director: it fits how your program already runs, and your program's money never passes through us. When you need help, you'll hear from someone who has run a program.
story.text_012: Along the way, I kept coming back to my favorite part of teaching: watching students grow. So Program Partner doesn't stop at the office work. Skill Pathways gives students clear steps to work toward and gives directors a quick way to check off progress. Practice logs help students and families see the work adding up between rehearsals. And
story.text_015: , our free practice site, is open to any band, orchestra or choir student, with no sign-in. Bringing the business side of a program and the student-growth side together in one place is what I always wanted as a director, and it's the part I'm proudest of.
story.text_016: I can't give anyone more hours in the day, but I can help give a few of them back to teaching.

team.heading: Meet the team
team.intro: A music director and an engineer, building Program Partner together.

members.name: Trey English
members.title: Director of bands, Feagin Mill Middle School
members.bio: Trey designs Program Partner, personally onboards every new program, and is the person you'll meet when you schedule a demo. He runs his own band program on it every day, so new features get tested in a real band room first.

members.name: Andrew Casal
members.title: Full-stack engineer
members.bio: Andrew has spent about ten years building web applications with React, TypeScript, Node, Postgres and Supabase. He partners with Trey on Program Partner's code and security, with a focus on who can see and change which data. In November 2026 he led an access control review of the whole platform, testing as a director, parent and student in two test schools, then retested every fix.

believe.text_019: Your program's money goes straight to your program. We never hold it and never take a cut.
believe.text_020: Student information belongs to your school or program. We protect it and never sell it.
believe.text_021: Your records are yours. Export them any time, and we delete them when you leave.

company.text_026: See it with your own program in mind.
